title: Cultural Heritage Of India Tourism Infrastructure & Planning

questions.question: What is the role of culture in tourism?
questions.solution_html:
• Culture plays a vital role in tourism as it attracts visitors through traditions, heritage, art
  • festivals, and lifestyle of a destination. It helps promote local identity and enhances the
  • tourist experience while supporting cultural preservation.

  • a) Overuse of Natural Resources
  • Rapid tourism growth increases demand for water, energy, and land. In destinations like Goa
  • Beaches, excessive tourist inflow leads to water shortages and pressure on local resources.
  • b) Pollution

  • Water pollution from sewage and waste disposal
  • Noise pollution in crowded tourist spots
  • For example, backwater tourism in Alappuzha has faced challenges due to waste and fuel
  • discharge from houseboats.
  • c) Habitat Destruction and Biodiversity Loss
  • Construction of hotels, resorts, and infrastructure leads to deforestation and loss of wildlife
  • habitats. Sensitive ecosystems like Himalayan Region are particularly vulnerable.
  • d) Overcrowding (Overtourism)
  • Excessive tourist numbers exceed the carrying capacity of destinations, causing environmental
  • stress, erosion, and degradation of natural attractions.

questions.question: Describe the basics of Ayurveda.

questions.question: Why is risk sharing important in PPP?
questions.solution_html:
• Risk sharing is a core principle of Public–Private Partnerships (PPP) because it determines
  • whether a project is efficient, financially viable, and sustainable. In a PPP, risks are allocated
  • between the public sector and private sector in a way that each party handles the risks it is best
  • equipped to manage.
questions.final_answer: equipped to manage.
